data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 result is an artifact of the mutation-generation process having read the acceptance record: a test constrains only when the mutation generator is blind to the test's installation history, and the distribution is the signature of a generator that was not blind.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutation generator did not read the acceptance record and the 3/26 persists, the selection-effect claim is falsified.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the survivors are in the declared-data region, the generator's bias explanation fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a blinded generator produces the same distribution, the artifact claim is wrong.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 compile.py loss is in a region the generator's record-reading would have predicted, the exposure claim is confounded.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When the mutation generator has read the acceptance record, it produces mutations that are conditionally independent of the test's planted failures only in the declared-data region, where the registry's schema makes the test's expectation obvious. In the added-behavior region, the generator's knowledge of the record biases it toward mutations the test cannot catch, producing the 3/26 survivors as a selection effect rather than a constraint failure. The compile.py 1/9 loss is the single mutation where the generator's knowledge of the record was incomplete or irrelevant, so the test's descriptive nature was exposed. The 4/4 to 6/7 results are the generator's own care reproducing the author's care, not evidence of constraint.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
